title: Fingerprintless Console usage rollup with DP-safe aggregations and approximate joins
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Console dashboards and ad-hoc queries need high-cardinality usage signals (unique workspaces, route counts, distinct users by route) while we simultaneously harden PII/identifiers exposure. Full denormalized facts with raw identifiers cause compliance and storage concerns and slow backfills. Goal: build a compact, fingerprintless rollup layer that preserves pre-aggregation semantics for common Console queries using DP-safe sketches and approximate joins. This will be the canonical surface for cost/latency attribution dashboards, SLO reporting, and customer activity heatmaps without storing raw user identifiers.
motivation: Reduce amount of raw identifier churn in warehouse, meet privacy requirements for enterprise customers, lower storage and backfill costs, and provide consistent approximate metrics suitable for dashboards and anomaly detection. Supports Private deployments where customer policy disallows storing any global unique id in the data lake.
tech_notes: Design uses HLL++ for distinct workspace/user estimates, Count-Min Sketch for heavy-hitter routes, and a compact route-time shard fact keyed by tenant-hash (salted) + hour + route_signature

Differential privacy layer: Laplace noise injection post-aggregation with per-workspace epsilon budget tracking and a configurable global minimum threshold to avoid noisy results for low-volume tenants
Approximate join strategy: use precomputed sketch fingerprints and bloom filters to approximate cross-entity joins (route -> model_variant) with conservative union cardinality corrections
Storage format: Iceberg ORC with partitioning on date and coarse region and sort-order on tenant_hash + hour to enable efficient compaction and time-range reads
Backfill approach: seed HLL/CMS state from existing invocation logs using single-pass mapper jobs, persisting sketch states as base tables to allow incremental merges
Cost trade-offs: smaller storage but higher CPU for sketch merges on reads; plan to pre-merge common 7/30-day windows to reduce query-time cost
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed; validated HLL error rates on production sample (error ~1.8% at 1M cardinality with 16k registers)
2026-02-19: Security reviewed sketch approach; confirmed safe if raw ids are hashed with per-tenant salt and salt rotation is audited
2026-02-24: Prototype ETL job that emits hourly sketches landed (PR: github.com/redwood/etl/pull/312)
2026-03-03: Console dashboard queries updated to use sketch-based estimates for the weekly-unique-users widget (A/B compare to raw counts), observed median variance <2.5% on active tenants
2026-03-10: Decided on DP epsilon baseline (0.5 per tenant per 30d window) after consult with privacy SME; added thresholding for tenants with fewer than 50 invocations/hour
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard widgets (weekly unique users, route active counts, route top-k) must match raw-count baselines within defined error bounds for >90% of tenants
No raw user identifiers written to any new rollup tables; audit logs show hashing + salt application in ETL
Backfill of last 90 days completes without exceeding budgeted EMR/compute by >20%
DP noise controls and epsilon accounting are implemented and covered by unit/integration tests
Query performance for top Console read patterns improves or is within 1.2x of current cost due to pre-merged windows
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Chose HLL++ over deterministic sampling because cardinality-sensitive metrics were critical for billing and SLOs
2026-02-19: Adopted per-tenant salted hashing to prevent cross-tenant correlation and accidental leakage
2026-02-28: Deferred sketching of embeddings/sem-search usage to separate follow-up ticket to reduce scope
2026-03-10: Locked DP epsilon to 0.5 and minimum reporting threshold of 50 invocations/hour after privacy review
dashboards_and_validations: Validation job: daily/validate_sketch_estimates (compares sketch estimates to sampled raw counts)
Grafana panels: per-tenant error histogram, sketch-merge-latency, backfill-progress, dp-epsilon-spend
Canary: enable sketch-based widgets for 5% of tenants and compare alerts for SLA regressions over 7 days
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): run sketch ETL in parallel with existing rollups; write sketches to new base tables and expose read-only sketch adapters to Console
Phase 2 (1 week): behind feature flag, swap dashboard reads for sketch-based adapters for low-risk widgets and measure variance and cost
Phase 3 (2 weeks): backfill 90d for all tenants, create pre-merged 7d and 30d windows; flip default reads once data quality gates pass
Rollback: retain legacy denorm facts for 30 days post-cutover and have read-path toggle in Console config
open_questions: How to handle billing use-cases that require exact per-invocation accounting for a subset of enterprise customers? (proposal: maintain exact-denorm for paid premium tenants only)
Will the DP epsilon budget be acceptable for customers undergoing repeated ad-hoc analysis? Need policy for on-demand higher-precision exports
Edge case: multi-route invocations in the same request — how to avoid double-counting with conservative union corrections?
